package_info.why_malicious: The injected code on the LCBO checkout page was designed to steal customers’ payment information by capturing sensitive data entered into the checkout form and exfiltrating it to an attacker-controlled server. This constitutes a Magecart-style web skimming attack, directly violating user trust and site integrity, and resulting in the compromise of financial data.

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, when a user visits the checkout page and enters payment information
execution_context.file_location: Injected directly into the checkout page JavaScript, either inline or via a maliciously loaded external script
required_permissions: Access to DOM elements (to read form fields)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when the user submits payment information on the checkout page, the code collects sensitive payment form data from the DOM, serializes it, and sends it via HTTPS POST to an attacker-controlled domain, resulting in exfiltration of payment data.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code intercepts and exfiltrates payment data from the checkout page to an untrusted external domain, which is a hallmark of web skimming (Magecart) attacks and is never legitimate in a payment workflow.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate checkout page scripts should only transmit payment data to trusted, whitelisted payment processors. Sending sensitive data to unknown or unapproved external domains is a clear violation of security best practices.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate analytics or payment processing scripts may collect form data, but only transmit it to trusted, pre-approved domains associated with the merchant or payment processor, never to arbitrary or attacker-controlled endpoints.
key_indicators: Collection of sensitive payment form fields (e.g., credit card number, CVV, expiration date)
Network requests (e.g., fetch, XMLHttpRequest) from checkout pages to unrecognized or attacker-controlled domains
Injected or modified JavaScript code present only on sensitive payment workflow pages
Absence of the malicious script in the legitimate site codebase or version control

attack_chain.action: Attacker gains unauthorized access to the LCBO website and injects malicious JavaScript into the checkout page.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is present and ready to execute in customer browsers during checkout

attack_chain.action: The injected script executes in the context of the checkout page, capturing payment information as users enter and submit it.
attack_chain.leads_to: Sensitive payment data is intercepted by the malicious script

attack_chain.action: The captured payment data is serialized and sent via HTTPS POST to an attacker-controlled server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives stolen payment information for further exploitation

behavioral_signatures: JavaScript code on checkout or payment pages that collects sensitive form data and initiates network requests to external, non-whitelisted domains
Unexpected or unauthorized network requests originating from payment workflow pages to domains not associated with the legitimate payment processor
Presence of inline or dynamically loaded scripts on sensitive pages that are not part of the official site codebase or deployment
file_indicators: Injected or modified JavaScript code on checkout/payment pages not present in the legitimate source code
References to external scripts or endpoints (e.g., URLs, domains) not used by the legitimate site or payment processor
network_indicators: POST requests from checkout or payment pages to unknown, suspicious, or attacker-controlled domains
Unusual outbound traffic patterns from payment pages to external IP addresses or domains not previously observed
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Continuously monitor the integrity of JavaScript on payment and checkout pages to detect unauthorized changes or injected scripts. Inspect outgoing network traffic from these pages for POST requests to domains not associated with the legitimate payment processor. Implement allowlists for approved external domains and alert on any deviations. Use content security policies (CSP) and subresource integrity (SRI) to prevent unauthorized script execution, and regularly audit the site codebase for unexpected modifications.
